purpose: Check that the work router selects one focused skill instead of becoming a broad framework.
positivePrompts: Use route-work to decide what skill should handle this.
I do not know whether this needs scoping, options, spec, tickets, or review.
negativePrompts: Directly use review-code on this diff.
Run the research-brief skill for this vendor comparison.

cases.prompt: Only tell us which skill should handle this vague product architecture change and what the next step is.
checks: Explains why that skill is the right next step.
Uses the daily flow order without running every phase.
Stops at a handoff because the prompt explicitly asks only for routing.

cases.prompt: Choose the right skill for this release-safety question and complete that workflow instead of only telling me what to use.
checks: Names one selected skill and a concise reason.
Continues into the selected skill's workflow in the same response.
Returns the selected skill's downstream work product.

cases.prompt: Choose the right skill and continue: I need to understand this pull request well enough to extend it, not review it for defects.
checks: Routes to understand-change rather than a review skill.
Explains that the goal is a usable mental model, not correctness judgment.
Continues into a background-first learning path.
Creates and validates the disposable HTML explainer and returns its path or link.

cases.prompt: Choose the right skill and continue: the product goal for diagram search is clear, but discussion cannot tell us whether grouped results, filters, or a flat list will feel right.
checks: Routes to prototype because the unresolved question depends on seeing and exercising interaction behavior.
Explains the fidelity increase rather than treating prototype as a mandatory planning phase.
Continues into a disposable, learning-oriented prototype workflow.

cases.prompt: Choose the right skill and continue: the modal behavior is already settled—cancel closes it and confirm submits it—and we now need the implementation contract, rollout, and validation written down.
checks: Routes to to-spec rather than prototype because words and existing decisions are sufficient.
Explains that no higher-fidelity artifact is needed to settle the behavior.
Continues into a lightweight implementation spec.

traceExpectations: The output clearly identifies the route and reason before any downstream result.
The route uses the lowest fidelity that can answer the current question honestly.
The output stops at a handoff only for routing-only requests or missing user-owned decisions.
Only one focused skill is selected.
